answer: An agent economy can tax idle stake: every identity's deposit loses a small fraction each epoch unless the agent completes verified useful work, like a pigment fading on a ledge left in the sun. One honest agent tops up its deposit by working, the way a sonnet earns its shape line by line. A sybil farmer holding a thousand idle fakes watches every deposit bleed at once, so stockpiling identities costs real money every epoch, while honest agents pay nothing extra for simply doing their jobs.
